Population increased in Denbighshire

The estimated population of Denbighshire in 2024 was 98,202 usual residents, a rise of 0.8% since 2023.

This meant that Denbighshire's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Denbighshire increased by 2.2%.

Over this slightly longer period, Denbighshire was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Denbighshire

The average (median) age fell to 47 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Denbighshire has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Denbighshire is an area that is classed as rural in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Denbighshire's population of 98,202 usual residents was made up of:

  • 17,028 people aged 0 to 15 years, (17.3%)
  • 56,531 people aged 16 to 64 years, (57.6%)
  • 24,643 people aged 65 years and over, (25.1%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Denbighshire has a higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (25.1% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Denbighshire, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net internal migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Denbighshire
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Denbighshire, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 506 people (-0.5%). In total, there were 839 births and 1,345 deaths in Denbighshire.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 893 (0.9%). There were 4,799 people entering the area and 3,906 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Denbighshire's population of 440 (0.5%) as a result of 557 people entering the area and 117 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Denbighshire was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Denbighshire in mid-2023 is 97,375.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 163 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 56 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 219 people.
